title: School voucher program on student test scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
I would use the Difference-in-Differences (DID) method for this analysis. This method compares the changes in outcomes over time between a treatment group and a control group. Here, "treated" indicates if a district is part of the voucher program, and "post" indicates the period post-introduction of the voucher program. The key assumption is the parallel trends assumption, meaning that in the absence of the treatment, the average difference in outcomes between treated and control groups would have remained constant over time.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s03_data.csv")

# Verify structure of the data
head(data)
str(data)

# Run the DID regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data=data)

# Summary of the regression model
summary(did_model)

# Coefficient of interest is treat_x_post
cat("Coefficient on treat_x_post (DID estimator):", 
    coef(summary(did_model))[["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]], "\n")

# Robust standard errors
coeftest(did_model, vcov = vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1"))

# Conduct basic robustness check by allowing for time fixed effects
robust_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post + factor(period), data=data)

# Summary of the robust model
summary(robust_model)

# Coefficient with time fixed effects
cat("Coefficient on treat_x_post (with period fixed effects):", 
    coef(summary(robust_model))[["treat_x_post", "Estimate"]], "\n")

# Robust standard errors for the robust model
coeftest(robust_model, vcov = vcovHC(robust_model, type = "HC1"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive sign for the coefficient on `treat_x_post`, indicating that the introduction of the school voucher program improved standardized test scores in the treated districts compared to control districts. The magnitude will depend on the effect size of the program but given typical educational interventions, a small to moderate increase (e.g., 0.1 to 0.5 standard deviations) could be expected. The robustness checks should maintain the sign and significance of this effect if the parallel trends assumption holds.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=voucher districts, control=non-voucher; shock=program introduction
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Test scores increase significantly in voucher districts after program launch
